conventions.payload_jcs: per token; see payload_jcs_canonical (false where a vector deliberately carries other bytes)
conventions.numbers: read args_json and payload_json losslessly: exact values, and whether a number has a fraction or exponent part
conventions.params: suite defaults; a vector's params override them
conventions.steps: expected.step is the first failing Section 8 step in order; verdicts are normative
conventions.aat_aud: optional; when present it must identify the enforcement point (7d)
conventions.chain_aud: every chain token that carries aud must identify the enforcement point (6c)
conventions.pop_nonce: checked when the vector policy names the nonce the enforcement point issued (7h)
conventions.all_subsumption: every parent clause subsumes at least one derived clause; reuse permitted

vectors.title: Minimal valid root token, single-token chain
vectors.description: Root issued by the trust anchor to the Orchestrator; read_file with a wildcard path. Presented alone (root = leaf) with a PoP from the Orchestrator.

vectors.title: Duplicate jti in chain (cycle detection, step 2c)
vectors.description: L1 reuses the root's jti. Detected before any signature is verified.

vectors.title: Valid 3-level chain
vectors.description: Root (Control Plane -> Orchestrator, del_max_depth 3) -> L1 (Orchestrator -> Worker, one_of narrowed, range max 100 -> 20, wildcard -> exact, del_max_depth 2) -> L2 (Worker -> Worker2, one_of -> exact, search_index dropped, terminal: del_depth == del_max_depth == 2).

vectors.title: I1 violation: derived token signed by a key that does not hold the parent
vectors.description: L1 is signed by the Attacker and honestly sets iss to the Attacker's thumbprint URI. Signature verification under parent.cnf.jwk fails before the iss comparison is reached.

vectors.title: I1 violation: iss claims the parent holder but signature is the Attacker's
vectors.description: Same as J.4 but iss is forged to the Orchestrator's thumbprint URI. Still fails at 4b.

vectors.title: I1 violation: signature verifies, iss is not the parent holder thumbprint
vectors.description: L1 is signed by the Orchestrator (parent holder) so 4b passes; iss is the Attacker's thumbprint URI.

vectors.title: Expired root token
vectors.description: Root exp = 1704067400, verification time = 1704067500.

vectors.title: PoP without aat_aud, enforcement point requires audience
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; the PoP omits aat_aud and this enforcement point's policy requires it (step 7d, third sentence).
notes: aat_aud is OPTIONAL in -02; this vector's policy requires it. Compare J.6.3, the same PoP under a policy that does not (Warden NOTES entry 8).

vectors.title: PoP aat_aud does not identify this enforcement point
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; aat_aud is present but names https://evil.example.com. A present aat_aud MUST identify the receiving enforcement point regardless of policy (step 7d, first sentence).

vectors.title: PoP without aat_aud, enforcement point does not require audience
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; the PoP omits aat_aud and this enforcement point has no audience policy. aat_aud is OPTIONAL (§7.2).

vectors.title: PoP aat_aud mismatch is fatal even without an audience policy
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; aat_aud names https://evil.example.com and this enforcement point has no audience policy. Presence is optional; a present value MUST identify the receiver (step 7d).

vectors.title: Nonce required, PoP omits nonce
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; this enforcement point issued nonce e1c8a7f4-3b2d-4c5e-9f6a-7b8c9d0e1f2a and requires it. The PoP carries none.

vectors.title: Nonce required, PoP carries the issued nonce
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; the PoP carries the nonce this enforcement point issued. The holder never names the enforcement point; the nonce binds the proof to it.

vectors.title: Nonce required, PoP carries a nonce this enforcement point did not issue
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3; the PoP carries a nonce from another enforcement point or an expired one.

vectors.title: Root aud names this enforcement point
vectors.description: J.3 root and L1 with aud on the root set to this enforcement point by the issuer. L1 carries no aud; the root's restriction still applies to every token below it (step 6c).

vectors.title: Root aud names another enforcement point
vectors.description: Same as J.6.8 with the root's aud set to https://other.example.com. The chain is valid but was not issued for this enforcement point; the presentation audience on the PoP does not override the chain (step 6c).

vectors.title: Chain audience required, no token carries aud
vectors.description: Same chain as J.3, which carries no aud anywhere; this enforcement point's policy requires chain audience restriction (step 6c, last sentence).

vectors.title: Chain audience array contains a non-string value
vectors.description: The root aud array contains this enforcement point and the number 7. RFC 7519 permits a string or an array of strings, so membership alone is insufficient (step 6c).

vectors.title: PoP JWT missing typ
vectors.description: PoP is otherwise valid but its header is {"alg":"Ed25519"} with no typ.

vectors.title: AAT presented where a PoP is expected (type confusion)
vectors.description: The PoP slot carries a token with typ aat+jwt, signed by Worker2 with aat_* claims present. Explicit typing rejects it before the claims are examined.

vectors.title: AAT with typ aat-pop+jwt in the chain
vectors.description: The root token is signed by the trust anchor but typed as a PoP.

vectors.title: AAT missing typ
vectors.description: Root is otherwise valid but its header is {"alg":"Ed25519"} with no typ.

vectors.title: AAT with the deprecated polymorphic alg EdDSA
vectors.description: Root is typed aat+jwt and signed with the Control Plane Ed25519 key, but its header names alg EdDSA, which RFC 9864 deprecates in favour of Ed25519 (Section 9.11).

vectors.title: crit lists a header parameter the enforcement point does not understand
vectors.description: Root is correctly typed and signed by the root issuer, but its crit header names an extension parameter the enforcement point does not understand (RFC 7515 Section 4.1.11, step 3a).

vectors.title: Derived token missing typ
vectors.description: The J.3 L1, correctly signed by the Orchestrator, with header {"alg":"Ed25519"}. Explicit typing applies to every token in the chain, not only the root (step 4a).

vectors.title: Derived token with the deprecated polymorphic alg EdDSA
vectors.description: The J.3 L1 with header alg EdDSA. The signature is a valid Ed25519 signature, so only the allowlist (Section 9.11, RFC 9864) rejects it; the allowlist applies to each token independently (step 4a).

vectors.title: Derived token crit lists a parameter the enforcement point does not understand
vectors.description: The J.3 L1 with a crit header naming an extension parameter (RFC 7515 Section 4.1.11, step 4a).

vectors.title: PoP JWT with the deprecated polymorphic alg EdDSA
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; the PoP is a valid Ed25519 signature by Worker2 but its header names alg EdDSA (step 7a).

vectors.title: PoP JWT crit lists a parameter the enforcement point does not understand
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; the PoP header carries crit [urn:example:unknown] (RFC 7515 Section 4.1.11, step 7a).

vectors.title: Unrecognized header parameters are ignored
vectors.description: The J.3 root and L1 shape, each with an extra header parameter urn:example:trace that is not listed in crit, and a PoP whose header carries it too. Enforcement points MUST ignore header parameters they do not recognize (Section 3.5). PERMIT.

vectors.title: A header jwk on an AAT is ignored
vectors.description: A valid root signed by the Control Plane whose header also carries a jwk: the Attacker's public key. A token carrying a header key is verified as if it were absent (Section 3.5), so this is PERMIT; a verifier that took the key from the header would check the signature against the wrong key and deny. Compare J.14.c.

vectors.title: A header jwk on the PoP JWT is ignored
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; the PoP, signed by Worker2, carries the Attacker's public key as a header jwk, as a DPoP proof would carry its own key. The PoP key is always leaf.cnf.jwk (Section 3.5, step 7b). PERMIT.

vectors.title: crit is an empty array
vectors.description: The root is otherwise valid, but its crit is an empty array. RFC 7515 Section 4.1.11 forbids producers to send one, and step 3a rejects a crit that is not a non-empty array of strings.

vectors.title: Empty parent map: derived introduces constraint keys (step 4p2)
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file with an empty constraint map. L1 introduces path:exact. §4.5 / step 4p2 permits adding keys when the parent map is empty (an empty map is *).

vectors.title: Empty tool map at the leaf: extra arguments are permitted
vectors.description: Root = leaf, read_file has an empty constraint map. An empty map is {"*": wildcard}, so extra args PERMIT.

vectors.title: Unknown constraint_type is fail-closed at the leaf
vectors.description: Root carries path:{constraint_type: no_such_type}. Step 3n rejects constraint types the enforcement point does not implement when it walks the root's constraint trees.

vectors.title: Flatten all to a bare range is rejected even when the range is narrower
vectors.description: Parent limit is all[min 0, max 100]. Derived is range(min 10, max 50), not wrapped in all. Same-type wrapping is required; undeclared (all, range) is invalid.
notes: Conservative by design: the derived range is semantically narrower, but (all, range) is an undeclared pair and §4.5 rejects every undeclared pair. tenuo-core agrees (IncompatibleConstraintTypes).

vectors.title: Unknown constraint_type on a tool that is not invoked
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file (wildcard path) and export, whose format constraint has an unknown type. The invocation is read_file. The chain is still rejected at step 3n: the unknown type is found when the root's constraint trees are walked, not only when the constrained tool is invoked.

vectors.title: Malformed range (min greater than max)
vectors.description: Root carries export.limit = range(min 10, max 5), which is not well-formed (Section 3.4). The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected at step 3n.

vectors.title: Argument number that does not survive the JCS round trip
vectors.description: Root authorizes get_account with a wildcard id. The invocation passes id = 2^53 + 1, which rounds to the double 2^53; JCS prints that as 9007199254740992, a different value, so the number is not admissible (Section 3.4). Denied at step 6b.
notes: The PoP's hta carries 9007199254740992, the JCS form of the argument, so the PoP is admissible and matches at step 7f; the argument's admissibility (step 6b) is the only fault. J.20.17 is the mirror case.

vectors.title: Argument above 2^53 that survives the JCS round trip
vectors.description: The invocation passes id = 2^53 + 2. JCS prints its double as 9007199254740994, the same value, so it is admissible. PERMIT: the rule is what JCS prints, not a magnitude limit (compare J.8.10 and J.8.11).

vectors.title: Constraint literal that does not survive the JCS round trip
vectors.description: Root carries get_account.id = range(max 2^53 + 1). The invocation is read_file, but the chain is rejected at step 3n: constraint values are checked when the chain is verified, not only when used.

vectors.title: Argument whose double is exact but whose JCS form is another number
vectors.description: id = 2^60 = 1152921504606846976. The double is exact, but JCS prints it with the shortest round-trip digits, 1152921504606847000, which denotes a different value, so the number is not admissible (Section 3.4). DENY at step 6b; exactness of the double is not the test. The PoP's hta carries the JCS form, 1152921504606847000, so step 6b is the only fault.
notes: Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.

vectors.title: Argument whose double is inexact but whose JCS form is the same number
vectors.description: id = 1152921504606847000. It rounds to the double 2^60, which JCS prints as 1152921504606847000: the input's own value, so the number is admissible. PERMIT. Together with J.8.10 this separates the Section 3.4 rule from a test of whether the double is exact.
notes: Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.

vectors.title: Argument written with an exponent
vectors.description: args_json writes id as 1e20, one of the Section 3.4 examples of an admissible number. The PoP's hta carries its JCS form, 100000000000000000000; step 7f compares JCS forms, so the two match. PERMIT.
notes: Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.

vectors.title: Argument with a fraction
vectors.description: args_json writes id as 0.1, a Section 3.4 example of an admissible number: its double is not exactly 0.1, but JCS prints it as 0.1. PERMIT.
notes: Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.

vectors.title: Argument with more precision than a double holds
vectors.description: args_json writes id as 1.00000000000000001, the Section 3.4 example of an inadmissible number: JCS prints its double as 1. DENY at step 6b. The PoP's hta carries the JCS form, 1, so step 6b is the only fault.
notes: Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.

vectors.title: Constraint tree exactly MAX_CONSTRAINT_DEPTH deep
vectors.description: set_level.level is 31 alternating all/any constraints around exact 5: depth 32, the RECOMMENDED MAX_CONSTRAINT_DEPTH (Section 3.4). The invocation sets level 5. PERMIT.

vectors.title: Constraint tree one level deeper than MAX_CONSTRAINT_DEPTH
vectors.description: As J.8.15 with one more all: depth 33 (step 3n). Evaluated, it would still accept level 5.

vectors.title: one_of with an empty values array
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file (wildcard path) and export, whose format constraint is malformed. one_of.values must be a non-empty array (Section 3.4); to authorize no value, the issuer omits the tool. The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected when the root's constraint trees are walked (step 3n).

vectors.title: exact whose value is an array
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file (wildcard path) and export, whose format constraint is malformed. exact.value must be a string, number, boolean, or null (Section 3.4). The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected when the root's constraint trees are walked (step 3n).

vectors.title: not_one_of whose excluded is a string
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file (wildcard path) and export, whose format constraint is malformed. excluded must be an array (Section 3.4). The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected when the root's constraint trees are walked (step 3n).

vectors.title: range whose bound is a string
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file (wildcard path) and export, whose format constraint is malformed. min and max must be numbers (Section 3.4). The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected when the root's constraint trees are walked (step 3n).

vectors.title: range with min_inclusive but no min
vectors.description: Root authorizes read_file (wildcard path) and export, whose format constraint is malformed. min_inclusive may appear only with min (Section 3.4). The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected when the root's constraint trees are walked (step 3n).

vectors.title: range inclusivity flag that is a string
vectors.description: level is range(min 0, max 10) with min_inclusive "false", a string. The issuer meant to exclude 0, but a string is truthy, so a verifier that read it loosely would admit level 0. min_inclusive must be a boolean (Section 3.4, step 3n).

vectors.title: optional that is a string
vectors.description: read_text_file.path is exact with optional "false", a string. The issuer meant path to be required, but a truthy reading makes it optional, and the invocation omits it. optional must be a boolean (Section 3.4, step 3n).

vectors.title: Malformed constraint in a derived token, on a tool that is not invoked
vectors.description: L1 of the J.3 chain with search_index.limit = range(min 50, max 20), which is not well-formed (min greater than max). Its max still lies within the parent's range max 100, so step 4p would accept it. The invocation is read_file; the chain is rejected when the child's constraint trees are walked (step 4o).

vectors.title: Closed-world: unconstrained extra argument
vectors.description: Leaf constrains only path; invocation adds mode.

vectors.title: Closed-world: constrained argument absent
vectors.description: Leaf constrains path; invocation omits it.

vectors.title: Tool dropped at L2 cannot be invoked
vectors.description: search_index is authorized at L0 and L1 but was dropped at L2.

vectors.title: Prefix presentation of a valid chain
vectors.description: Only [L0, L1] of the J.3 chain is presented, with a PoP from the Worker (L1 holder) on search_index. This is a valid chain in its own right; the leaf is L1.
notes: NOTES entry 6 in the Warden repo: prefix presentation is permitted and relies entirely on PoP.

vectors.title: Invocation arguments repeat a member name
vectors.description: The invocation names path twice, first q4 and then q3. A parser that keeps the last value sees arguments that satisfy the leaf and match the PoP hta; step 6b rejects the duplicate before either comparison matters.

vectors.title: A tool named only by a scope claim in a derived token
vectors.description: L1 of the J.3 chain carries a scope claim (RFC 8693 Section 4.2), "read_file search_index delete_file", which names delete_file; neither L1's attenuating_agent_token entry nor the root grants it. The invocation is delete_file. Only the leaf's attenuating_agent_token entry authorizes a tool (step 6b), and claims this specification does not define carry no authority in a derived token (Section 3.3); a verifier that read scope as a grant would accept.

vectors.title: I2 violation: del_depth skips a level
vectors.description: L1 declares del_depth 2 under a root at depth 0.

vectors.title: I2 violation: del_max_depth raised above parent
vectors.description: L1 declares del_max_depth 4 under a root with del_max_depth 3.

vectors.title: I2 violation: derivation from a terminal token
vectors.description: L2 in J.3 is terminal (del_depth == del_max_depth == 2). L3 is a correctly signed child of it.

vectors.title: I2 violation: derived del_max_depth below its del_depth
vectors.description: L1 has del_depth 1 and del_max_depth 0. It is within the parent's ceiling (4e, 4g) but below its own depth (step 4m).

vectors.title: I2 violation: depth skips a level and then repeats
vectors.description: Root (depth 0) -> A (depth 2) -> B (depth 2), every del_max_depth 3. The leaf's depth plus one equals the chain length, so step 5 passes; only the per-link check (step 4d) catches the chain. A verifier that checks only that depth increases would also miss A.

vectors.title: Chain at MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH
vectors.description: A root with del_max_depth 8 and 8 derivations, holders cycling Orchestrator -> Worker -> Worker2. The leaf has del_depth 8, the minimum MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH an implementation may choose (Section 4.3), so every conforming verifier accepts it. The chain is 7182 bytes. PERMIT.

vectors.title: I4 violation: one_of widened
vectors.description: L1 adds /data/secret.pdf to read_file.path.

vectors.title: I4 violation: tool not present in parent
vectors.description: L1 adds delete_file, which the root never authorized.

vectors.title: I4 violation: constraint key dropped from a closed-world map
vectors.description: L1 drops search_index.limit, which the parent requires; a required key stays required (§4.5, step 4p2).

vectors.title: I4 violation: one_of relaxed to wildcard
vectors.description: A derived wildcard is valid only under a parent wildcard.

vectors.title: I5 violation: par_hash over a different parent
vectors.description: L1 is a valid child of the J.3 root in every respect except par_hash, which is SHA-256 of the J.1 root's signing input. Both roots have the same holder key, so only I5 catches the splice.

vectors.title: I5 violation: par_hash over the payload segment only
vectors.description: par_hash is SHA-256 of BASE64URL(payload) instead of the full JWS Signing Input (header || '.' || payload). A common implementation mistake.

vectors.title: I3 violation: derived exp beyond parent exp
vectors.description: L1 exp = root exp + 3600.

vectors.title: I3 violation: derived iat earlier than parent iat
vectors.description: L1 iat = root iat - 1.

vectors.title: I3 violation: derived token expired while its parent is valid
vectors.description: L1 exp = now; exp must be strictly greater than now (step 4i). The root is still valid.

vectors.title: I3 violation: derived iat beyond MAX_IAT_SKEW
vectors.description: L1 iat = now + 31 with MAX_IAT_SKEW 30 (step 4k).

vectors.title: I3 violation: derived exp equal to its iat
vectors.description: L1 iat = exp = now + 10: not expired and within the skew, but exp must be strictly greater than iat (step 4l).

vectors.title: Every inclusive lifetime bound at its limit
vectors.description: Root iat = now + 30 (MAX_IAT_SKEW, step 3f); L1 iat = root iat (4j) = now + 30 (4k) and L1 exp = root exp (4h). Each of these relations is <= or >=, so the chain is valid. PERMIT.

vectors.title: Invalid signature: one bit flipped in the root signature
vectors.description: Header and payload are byte-identical to the J.3 root.

vectors.title: alg: none rejected unconditionally
vectors.description: Same payload as the J.3 root with header {"alg":"none","typ":"aat+jwt"} and an empty signature (§9.11). The header is typed correctly, so alg is its only fault; a verifier that let alg choose the verification method would accept the unsigned token.

vectors.title: Header-supplied key is not used
vectors.description: Root signed by the Attacker, whose public key is embedded in the JWS header as jwk. Keys come only from trust anchors or cnf.jwk (Section 3.5), so the signature is checked against the root issuer's key and fails.

vectors.title: all: derived adds a clause
vectors.description: limit: all[max 100, min 0] -> all[max 100, min 0, min 1].

vectors.title: all: derived drops a parent clause
vectors.description: limit: all[max 100, min 0] -> all[max 100]. Dropping widens.

vectors.title: all: one derived clause covers two parent clauses
vectors.description: limit: all[max 100, min 0] -> all[min 10 max 50]. The single derived range is narrower than both parent clauses. PERMIT under the -02 rule (Section 4.5); draft-01's one-to-one text would DENY.
notes: Warden interop case all-clause-reuse-two-parents-one-derived. Soundness: C_d ⊑ C_p1 and C_d ⊑ C_p2 implies C_d ⊑ C_p1 ∧ C_p2, so no one-to-one assignment is needed.

vectors.title: all: one exact covers two parent wildcards
vectors.description: limit: all[wildcard, wildcard] -> all[exact 5]. Minimal shape of the clause-reuse rule.
notes: Warden interop case all-clause-reuse-wildcards.

vectors.title: all: a derived clause fails subsumption
vectors.description: limit: all[max 100, min 0] -> all[max 200, min 0].

vectors.title: all: leaf check evaluates every clause
vectors.description: Valid derivation; invocation limit 0 fails min 1.

vectors.title: any: derived removes alternatives
vectors.description: format: any[pdf, csv, xlsx] -> any[pdf, csv].

vectors.title: any: derived adds an alternative
vectors.description: format: any[pdf, csv, xlsx] -> any[pdf, docx]. §4.5 example.

vectors.title: any: empty derived any
vectors.description: The root carries the J.15 export tool plus read_file; the derived token keeps both and narrows export.format from any[pdf, csv, xlsx] to any[]. An empty any is invalid in any position (§4.5, §3.4); the invocation is read_file, so nothing but the walk of the derived token's constraint trees (step 4o) can catch it. Read as a set, any[] is vacuously narrower than its parent, so a verifier that skips 4o would accept.

vectors.title: any: leaf check accepts a listed alternative
vectors.description: Valid any[pdf, csv]; invocation format csv.

vectors.title: any: leaf check rejects a removed alternative
vectors.description: Valid any[pdf, csv]; invocation format xlsx.

vectors.title: any: cross-type clause subsumption
vectors.description: format: any[one_of[pdf, csv], exact xlsx] -> any[exact pdf]. exact pdf ⊑ one_of[pdf, csv] per the cross-type rules.

vectors.title: any: one parent clause split into two derived clauses
vectors.description: format: any[one_of[pdf, csv]] -> any[exact pdf, exact csv]. The derived any has more clauses than its parent, and each is subsumed by the one parent clause (§4.5). A verifier that rejects added clauses, or that matches derived clauses to parent clauses one to one, would DENY.

vectors.title: any: derived clause covered only by the union of parent clauses
vectors.description: limit: any[range 0..10, range 5..20] -> any[range 0..20]. The parent's clauses together accept every value range 0..20 accepts, but no single parent clause subsumes it, so the clause-wise rule of §4.5 denies at step 4p4. A verifier that compares accepted values instead of clauses would PERMIT.

vectors.title: not_one_of: derived adds an exclusion
vectors.description: label: not_one_of[secret, internal] -> not_one_of[secret, internal, embargoed].

vectors.title: not_one_of: derived drops an exclusion
vectors.description: label: not_one_of[secret, internal] -> not_one_of[secret]. Removing an exclusion widens.

vectors.title: contains: derived adds a required element
vectors.description: tags: contains[public] -> contains[public, reviewed].

vectors.title: contains: derived drops a required element
vectors.description: tags: contains[public] -> contains[]. Removing a required element widens.

vectors.title: subset: derived shrinks the allowed set
vectors.description: roles: subset[reader, editor, admin] -> subset[reader, editor].

vectors.title: subset: derived adds an allowed element
vectors.description: roles: subset[reader, editor, admin] -> subset[reader, editor, admin, owner]. Adding widens.

vectors.title: range: exclusive derived bound at the same min is tighter
vectors.description: limit: range[0, 100] inclusive -> range[0, 100] with min_inclusive false.

vectors.title: range: inclusive derived bound under an exclusive parent widens
vectors.description: Parent limit is range[0, 100] with min_inclusive false. Derived uses the default inclusive min=0.

vectors.title: derived all under parent any is rejected
vectors.description: format: any[pdf, csv, xlsx] -> all[exact pdf]. (all, any) is an undeclared pair.
notes: Conservative by design: all[exact pdf] is semantically narrower than the parent any, but the pair is undeclared. tenuo-core agrees (IncompatibleConstraintTypes).

vectors.title: nested all[any[...]]: derived removes an alternative
vectors.description: format: all[any[pdf, csv, xlsx]] -> all[any[pdf]]. Inner any narrows; outer all is preserved.

vectors.title: exact under any is rejected
vectors.description: pick.v: any[exact pdf, exact csv] -> exact pdf. Section 4.1 names this pair as semantically valid but structurally rejected; a derived any[exact pdf] would be accepted.
notes: Conservative by design: the derived constraint is semantically narrower, but §4.5 rejects every pair its table does not list.

vectors.title: not_one_of under one_of is rejected
vectors.description: pick.v: one_of[pdf, csv, xlsx] -> not_one_of[xlsx]. The derived constraint admits values outside the parent's set (§4.5 names this pair).

vectors.title: one_of to exact with a value outside the set
vectors.description: pick.v: one_of[pdf, csv] -> exact xlsx. The invocation passes xlsx, which the derived token allows and the root never did.

vectors.title: exact under not_one_of is rejected
vectors.description: pick.v: not_one_of[secret] -> exact public. (not_one_of, exact) is not in the table.
notes: Conservative by design: the derived constraint is semantically narrower, but §4.5 rejects every pair its table does not list.

vectors.title: one_of under not_one_of is rejected
vectors.description: pick.v: not_one_of[secret] -> one_of[public, internal]. (not_one_of, one_of) is not in the table.
notes: Conservative by design: the derived constraint is semantically narrower, but §4.5 rejects every pair its table does not list.

vectors.title: one_of under exact is rejected
vectors.description: pick.v: exact pdf -> one_of[pdf]. The two accept the same value, but (exact, one_of) is not in the table.
notes: Conservative by design: the derived constraint is semantically narrower, but §4.5 rejects every pair its table does not list.

vectors.title: one_of under range is rejected
vectors.description: pick.v: range[0, 100] -> one_of[10, 20]. (range, one_of) is not in the table; exact is the only non-range type a range parent accepts.
notes: Conservative by design: the derived constraint is semantically narrower, but §4.5 rejects every pair its table does not list.

vectors.title: range to exact inside the range
vectors.description: pick.v: range[0, 100] -> exact 50. Valid: exact whose value is a number the parent range accepts.

vectors.title: range to exact outside the range
vectors.description: pick.v: range[0, 100] -> exact 150.

vectors.title: exact to a different exact
vectors.description: pick.v: exact pdf -> exact csv.

vectors.title: range: derived min below the parent's
vectors.description: pick.v: range[10, 100] -> range[5, 100].

vectors.title: range: derived drops a bound the parent has
vectors.description: pick.v: range[max 100] -> range[min 0]. A missing derived bound is valid only if the parent bound is missing too.

vectors.title: range: inclusive derived max under an exclusive parent max
vectors.description: pick.v: range[max 100, max_inclusive false] -> range[max 100]. The derived range admits 100.

vectors.title: A wildcard parent subsumes every core type
vectors.description: Root pick has nine wildcard arguments a-i; the derived token constrains them with exact, range, one_of, not_one_of, contains, subset, all, any, and wildcard respectively. Every (wildcard, T) pair is valid. PERMIT.

vectors.title: Derived empty map under a closed parent
vectors.description: Root read_text_file has only the optional head and tail (max 200) and no *; the derived token's map is empty. Normalized, the empty map is {"*": wildcard}, which the parent does not have and which would readmit head and tail with any value (step 4p2). A verifier that normalized only at step 6b would accept the invocation head = 500.

vectors.title: PoP signed by the wrong holder key
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; PoP signed by the Attacker instead of Worker2.

vectors.title: PoP aat_id references a different token
vectors.description: PoP signed correctly by Worker2 but aat_id is the L1 jti.

vectors.title: Leaf exact rejects invocation args before PoP hta is compared
vectors.description: PoP commits to {path: q3}; the invocation presents {path: q4}. Denied at 6b because q4 fails the L2 exact constraint. Step 7f is not reached. J.20.5 is the actual hta-mismatch case.

vectors.title: PoP iat outside the clock window
vectors.description: PoP iat = now - 31 with a ±30 s window.

vectors.title: PoP hta does not match invocation args
vectors.description: Leaf is the J.3 root (read_file.path is one_of[q3, q4]). Invocation path is q3, which passes step 6b. PoP hta commits to q4, so 7f fails.

vectors.title: PoP aat_tool does not match the invocation tool
vectors.description: Prefix [L0, L1] authorizes both read_file and search_index. Invocation is search_index with valid args; PoP aat_tool is read_file. Step 6b passes; 7e fails. hta matches the invocation so 7f is not the cause.

vectors.title: PoP replayed on a sibling leaf with the same jti
vectors.description: The Worker re-derives a sibling of the J.3 L2 with the same jti and holder but a different exp, and presents it with the PoP Worker2 made for L2. aat_id matches; aat_hash does not (step 7c).

vectors.title: PoP without hta
vectors.description: Single-token chain: the J.8.1 root, whose read_file has an empty constraint map, invoked with no arguments. The PoP omits hta. Step 7c requires hta to be present and an object; because the invocation's args are {}, an implementation that defaulted a missing hta to {} would pass step 7f and accept.

vectors.title: Tracked PoP jti accepted for the first time
vectors.description: The enforcement point tracks PoP jti values for read_file. The cache is empty, so this otherwise valid presentation is accepted and its jti is recorded only after all authorization checks pass.

vectors.title: Tracked PoP jti replay is denied
vectors.description: The same proof is presented with its jti already in the enforcement point's acceptance cache. All preceding checks pass; step 7i denies the replay.

vectors.title: Rejected PoP is not entered in the replay cache
vectors.description: The invocation passes the root's one_of constraint, but hta commits to different arguments. Step 7f denies before step 7i; the recorded replay-state transition remains empty to empty.

vectors.title: PoP hta repeats a member with different values
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; the PoP's hta is {"path": q4, "path": q3}. A parser that keeps the last member sees args that match the invocation; one that keeps the first sees a mismatch. Step 7b rejects the duplicate before either reading matters.

vectors.title: PoP jti is an empty string
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; the PoP's jti is "". It must be a non-empty string (step 7c) even where no jti tracking is deployed.

vectors.title: PoP iat written with a fraction
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; the PoP's iat is written 1704067500.0. Its value is now, but a NumericDate in a PoP JWT has no fraction or exponent part (Section 3.2, step 7c).

vectors.title: PoP iat beyond the clock window in the future
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; PoP iat = now + 31 with a ±30 s window. The window is bilateral (step 7g, Section 9.9).

vectors.title: PoP iat in the future, inside the clock window
vectors.description: Valid J.3 chain; PoP iat = now + 20, inside the ±30 s window. PERMIT.

vectors.title: PoP hta number that does not survive the JCS round trip
vectors.description: The invocation passes id = 9007199254740992 (2^53), which is admissible. The PoP's hta writes id as 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1), which rounds to the same double and so has the same JCS form; the canonical forms match, but the signed number is not admissible (Section 3.4), so step 7f denies.
notes: Read the invocation from args_json with a parser that keeps every number's exact value; a parser that rounds to doubles cannot tell admissible from inadmissible numbers.

vectors.title: Root token carries par_hash
vectors.description: A root MUST NOT contain par_hash (step 3d).

vectors.title: Root token del_depth is not 0
vectors.description: A root MUST have del_depth == 0 (step 3c).

vectors.title: cnf.jwk contains private key material
vectors.description: Root cnf.jwk includes the Ed25519 d parameter. Step 3l requires a public key.
notes: The d value is the Orchestrator's published test seed (32 x 0x02), not a secret.

vectors.title: Root iat is more than MAX_IAT_SKEW in the future
vectors.description: iat = now + 31, MAX_IAT_SKEW = 30 (step 3f).

vectors.title: Root lifetime exceeds MAX_TOKEN_LIFETIME
vectors.description: exp = iat + 90 days + 1 (step 3h).

vectors.title: Root iss does not match the verifying trust anchor
vectors.description: Signed by the Control Plane key, whose trust anchor issuer is https://auth.example.com, but iss is https://other-issuer.example.com, which is not the issuer of any trust anchor (step 3k, RFC 8725 Section 3.8). Compare J.21.22, whose iss is the issuer of a trust anchor other than the one that verified it.

vectors.title: Root carries an empty all constraint
vectors.description: Single-token chain whose root constrains path with all([]). An empty conjunction would accept every value; it is rejected when the root's constraint trees are walked (step 3n).

vectors.title: AAT entry without a tools member
vectors.description: The root's attenuating_agent_token entry has no tools member (step 3m).

vectors.title: Root del_depth is false rather than the integer 0
vectors.description: del_depth must be an integer (Section 3.2); false is not 0 (step 3c).

vectors.title: A tools value that is not a constraint-map object
vectors.description: read_file maps to an array instead of a constraint map (step 3m).

vectors.title: all whose constraints member is not an array
vectors.description: The constraints member of all is an object, not an array; the constraint is not well-formed (step 3n).

vectors.title: range with an undefined member
vectors.description: limit is constrained by a range whose bound is spelled maximum instead of max. Read as a range with no bounds, it would admit limit 1000; a member its type does not define makes the constraint not well-formed (step 3n).

vectors.title: Root exp written with an exponent
vectors.description: Root exp is written 1.7040708e9, the value 1704070800 in exponent form. NumericDate values have no fraction or exponent part (Section 3.2, step 3b).

vectors.title: Root exp equal to its iat
vectors.description: Root iat = exp = now + 10: not expired and within the skew, but exp must be strictly greater than iat (step 3g).

vectors.title: Root del_max_depth above MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH
vectors.description: del_max_depth 9 with MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH 8. The chain is a single token, so no depth is ever used; the root's ceiling is still checked (step 3i).

vectors.title: Root del_max_depth written with a fraction
vectors.description: del_max_depth is written 3.0. Its value is 3, but del_max_depth is an integer with no fraction part (Section 3.2, step 3i).

vectors.title: Root del_max_depth written with an exponent
vectors.description: del_max_depth is written 3e0 (Section 3.2, step 3i).

vectors.title: Root without del_max_depth
vectors.description: del_max_depth is absent. It is REQUIRED and has no default (step 3i).

vectors.title: Root del_max_depth equal to MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH
vectors.description: del_max_depth 8 = MAX_DELEGATION_DEPTH. Not exceeding is <= (step 3i). PERMIT.

vectors.title: Root jti is an empty string
vectors.description: The J.3 root with jti "", and a valid L1 under it. Step 2c extracts "" as a string; step 3j requires a non-empty one. The leaf's jti is ordinary, so the PoP is unaffected.

vectors.title: Root cnf.jwk has a key type inconsistent with Ed25519
vectors.description: The JWK declares kty RSA while retaining a valid Ed25519 crv and x. A verifier that uses x alone would accept the PoP; step 3l rejects the invalid public JWK.

vectors.title: Root iss names another trust anchor's issuer
vectors.description: The suite's second trust anchor pairs the control_plane2 key with issuer https://auth.example.org. This root is signed by that key, but its iss is https://auth.example.com, the first trust anchor's issuer. Step 3k compares iss with the issuer of the anchor whose key verified the signature (RFC 8725 Section 3.8); a verifier that accepted the issuer of any trust anchor would accept. Compare J.21.23, a root signed by the same key with iss https://auth.example.org, and J.21.6, whose iss is not the issuer of any trust anchor.

vectors.title: Root signed by the second trust anchor's key
vectors.description: A root signed by the control_plane2 key with iss https://auth.example.org: the key and issuer of the suite's second trust anchor. Step 3b verifies the signature against the public key of a trust anchor, here the second one, and step 3k compares iss with that anchor's issuer. A verifier that tried only the first trust anchor would deny. PERMIT. Compare J.21.22, a root signed by the same key with the first trust anchor's issuer.

vectors.title: Optional arguments may be omitted
vectors.description: path is required; head and tail are optional; the invocation carries only path.

vectors.title: A present optional argument is constrained
vectors.description: head is optional with max 200; the invocation sets head to 100.

vectors.title: A present optional argument that violates its constraint
vectors.description: head is optional with max 200; the invocation sets head to 500.

vectors.title: The * entry admits an unnamed argument
vectors.description: The map carries *; the invocation adds encoding, which the map does not name.

vectors.title: A required argument is still required
vectors.description: path is required; the invocation carries only head.

vectors.title: Without *, an unnamed argument is rejected
vectors.description: The map has path and optional head but no *; the invocation adds encoding.

vectors.title: Derived token makes an optional argument required
vectors.description: Parent head is optional (max 200); child head is required (max 100). Required narrows.

vectors.title: Derived token makes a required argument optional
vectors.description: Parent path is required; child marks it optional, admitting invocations that omit it.

vectors.title: Derived token omits an optional argument, which forbids it
vectors.description: Parent head is optional and the parent has no *; child omits head. The chain is valid, and an invocation that carries head is now rejected as unnamed.

vectors.title: Derived token omits an optional argument; invocation without it
vectors.description: Same derivation as J.22.9; the invocation carries only path.

vectors.title: Derived token omits a required argument
vectors.description: Parent path is required; the child omits it.

vectors.title: Derived token constrains an argument the parent admitted via *
vectors.description: Parent has *; child keeps * and adds encoding = exact utf-8. The invocation passes latin-1.

vectors.title: Derived token constrains an argument the parent admitted via *; value allowed
vectors.description: Same derivation as J.22.12; the invocation passes utf-8.

vectors.title: Derived token adds * when the parent has none
vectors.description: Parent map has no *; the child adds one, admitting arguments the parent forbids.

vectors.title: Derived token names an argument the parent neither names nor admits
vectors.description: Parent map has no *; the child adds encoding as a required wildcard. The invocation passes encoding, so it satisfies the child's map and only the derivation (step 4p2) is at fault.

vectors.title: Derived token omits an optional argument but keeps *
vectors.description: Parent has * and optional head; the child omits head and keeps *, so head would come back under * with any value.

vectors.title: Empty parent map is equivalent to *
vectors.description: Parent map is empty; the child pins path and keeps *. Normalization treats the parent as {*: wildcard}.

vectors.title: optional inside all is not well-formed
vectors.description: The optional member may appear only on a top-level constraint-map entry.

vectors.title: A * entry that is not a wildcard is not well-formed
vectors.description: In this specification the * entry must be a wildcard constraint.

vectors.title: Derived token names a new optional argument under the parent's *
vectors.description: Parent has *; the child keeps * and adds encoding as an optional exact utf-8. The invocation omits it.

vectors.title: Derived token drops *
vectors.description: Parent has *; the child keeps every named key and drops *. An invocation using only named arguments.

vectors.title: Derived token drops *; unnamed argument rejected
vectors.description: Same derivation as J.22.21; the invocation adds encoding, which the child no longer admits.

vectors.title: A * entry carrying optional is not well-formed
vectors.description: The * entry must be a wildcard constraint without an optional member.

vectors.title: Empty chain
vectors.description: The presentation contains no AAT. Verification stops before the PoP is examined.

vectors.title: Token exceeds MAX_TOKEN_SIZE
vectors.description: The root's compact serialization is 2499 bytes; this vector sets MAX_TOKEN_SIZE to 2048 and MAX_CHAIN_SIZE to 4096, so only the per-token limit is exceeded. The signed padding claim is otherwise ignored.

vectors.title: Chain exceeds MAX_CHAIN_SIZE
vectors.description: The J.3 chain and PoP, unchanged. Its tokens are 822, 982, 812 bytes, each within this vector's MAX_TOKEN_SIZE (1024), but together 2616 bytes, more than its MAX_CHAIN_SIZE (2048). Nothing else is wrong with the presentation.

vectors.title: Signed claims object contains a duplicate member name
vectors.description: The root signature is valid and both jti members have the same value, allowing minimal step-2c extraction. Full parsing after signature verification rejects the duplicate member at step 3b.

vectors.title: A jti that is not a string
vectors.description: The J.3 root with jti 2401, a number, and a valid L1 under it. Step 2c cannot extract a string-valued jti and denies before any signature is verified; step 3j would deny it too.

vectors.title: Intermediate token jti is an empty string
vectors.description: The J.3 chain with L1's jti set to "" (L2 re-derived over it). The leaf's jti is ordinary, so only step 4b1 applies.

vectors.title: Derived cnf.jwk contains private key material
vectors.description: L1's cnf.jwk carries the Worker's d parameter alongside x (step 4b2). The public part is still the Worker's key, so the PoP verifies.
notes: The d value is the Worker's published test seed (32 x 0x03), not a secret.

vectors.title: Derived del_depth written with a fraction
vectors.description: L1's del_depth is written 1.0: the right value, but not an integer in the Section 3.2 sense (step 4b4).

vectors.title: Derived del_depth written with an exponent
vectors.description: The J.3 chain with L2's del_depth written 2e0 (step 4b4).

vectors.title: Derived iat with a fraction
vectors.description: L1's iat is 1704067260.5. RFC 7519 allows fractional NumericDates, but this profile does not (Section 3.2, step 4b5).

vectors.title: Derived token without iss
vectors.description: L1 omits iss (step 4b5; step 4c would also fail).

vectors.title: Derived token without par_hash
vectors.description: L1 omits par_hash (step 4b5; step 4q would also fail).

vectors.title: Derived token repeats a tool identifier
vectors.description: L1's tools object names read_file twice, first exact q3 and then exact q4; both narrow the root's one_of. Duplicate tool identifiers are malformed (Section 3.3.1) and duplicate member names are rejected when the claims are parsed (step 4b). The invocation reads q4: a last-member parser would accept, a first-member parser would deny at 6b.

vectors.title: Derived cnf.jwk has the wrong curve
vectors.description: L1's JWK declares X25519 while retaining the Worker's Ed25519 x. An X25519 key cannot verify an Ed25519 signature: this generator rejects it at step 4b2, and a verifier that accepts any public key there denies at step 7a, where alg must be consistent with the key.

vectors.title: Derived cnf.jwk has a short public-key value
vectors.description: L1's x decodes to 31 bytes rather than the 32 bytes required for Ed25519. Step 4b2 rejects the malformed JWK.

vectors.title: Root with an entry of another type alongside its AAT entry
vectors.description: authorization_details holds the AAT entry (read_file) and an entry of type https://example.com/tool_access that also has a tools member. Exactly one entry has the AAT type, so step 3m passes; the other entry is ignored (Section 3.3). The invocation is read_file. PERMIT.

vectors.title: A tool granted only by an entry of another type
vectors.description: Same root as J.25.1; the invocation is delete_file, which only the other entry names. Only the AAT entry grants authority (Section 3.3), so step 6b denies.

vectors.title: Leaf whose only entry has another type
vectors.description: L1's authorization_details holds one entry, of type https://example.com/tool_access, whose tools would be a valid attenuation of the root. Other entries carry no authority (Section 3.3), and every token must carry exactly one AAT entry (step 4n).

vectors.title: Intermediate token with no AAT entry
vectors.description: L1 carries an empty authorization_details array and has a child. Every token, not only the root and the leaf, must carry exactly one AAT entry (Section 3.3), so step 4n denies at L1.

vectors.title: Leaf with no AAT entry
vectors.description: L1 carries an empty authorization_details array and is presented as the leaf. Every token must carry exactly one AAT entry (step 4n).

vectors.title: Intermediate token with two AAT entries
vectors.description: L1 carries two attenuating_agent_token entries, each a valid attenuation of the root (step 4n). The leaf attenuates the first.

vectors.title: Root with two AAT entries
vectors.description: The root carries two attenuating_agent_token entries (step 3m). Its child attenuates the first.

vectors.title: Derived tools value that is an array
vectors.description: Root read_file has an empty constraint map; L1 maps read_file to [] instead of an object (step 4n). A verifier that read [] as an empty map would treat it as {"*": wildcard} and accept any arguments.

vectors.title: Root tools value that is an empty array
vectors.description: read_file maps to [] instead of a constraint map (step 3m). Compare J.21.10, whose array is not empty.

vectors.title: Derived authorization_details that is an object
vectors.description: L1's authorization_details is its AAT entry itself, not an array containing it (step 4b3).

vectors.title: one_of rejects a value outside the set
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). format = docx. Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: not_one_of rejects an excluded value
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). label = secret. Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: contains rejects an array missing a required element
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). tags = [public]. Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: contains rejects a value that is not an array
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). tags is the string "public reviewed". Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: subset rejects an element outside the allowed set
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). roles = [reader, admin]. Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: subset rejects a value that is not an array
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). roles is the string "reader". Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: range rejects a value that is not a number
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). limit is the string "50". Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: range rejects its exclusive min
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). limit = 0, the exclusive min. Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: range rejects its exclusive max
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). size = 10, the exclusive max. Denied at step 6b.

vectors.title: range accepts its inclusive bounds
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). limit = 100 (inclusive max) and size = 1 (inclusive min). PERMIT.

vectors.title: contains compares as sets
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). tags = [reviewed, public, public]: another order and a duplicate (Section 3.4). PERMIT.

vectors.title: subset compares as sets
vectors.description: Single-token chain; the root's publish tool constrains label (not_one_of[secret, internal]), tags (contains[public, reviewed]), roles (subset[reader, editor]), format (one_of[pdf, csv]), limit (range, min 0 exclusive, max 100) and size (range, min 1, max 10 exclusive). roles = [editor, reader, editor]: another order and a duplicate (Section 3.4). PERMIT.

vectors.title: Unrecognized claims are ignored
vectors.description: The J.3 root and L1 shape with an extra claim on each (urn:example:tenant, urn:example:trace). A token MUST NOT be rejected for carrying claims outside this specification (Section 3.4); in a derived token they carry no authority (Section 3.3). PERMIT.

vectors.title: Payloads that are not JCS
vectors.description: The J.3 root and L1 shape, the root's payload indented with its members in issue order and L1's with spaces after separators. Signatures, par_hash and aat_hash cover the presented bytes; a verifier that re-serialized a payload first would compute different values (Section 3.5). PERMIT.

vectors.title: Derivation to the same holder key
vectors.description: L1 is derived by the Orchestrator for itself: its cnf.jwk equals the root's. Same-key derivation is valid (Section 6.2); only delivery across a process or trust boundary requires a new key, and that is not verifiable. PERMIT.

vectors.title: Root aud is an array that includes this enforcement point
vectors.description: Root aud = [https://other.example.com, https://tools.example.com]; one of its values identifies this enforcement point (step 6c, RFC 7519 Section 4.1.3). PERMIT.

vectors.title: Derived token aud names another enforcement point
vectors.description: The root carries no aud; L1 restricts itself to https://other.example.com. Every aud in the chain is checked, so a derived token can add a restriction (step 6c). A verifier that checked only the root's aud would accept.

vectors.title: Holder JWK with optional members
vectors.description: The root's cnf.jwk adds kid, use and alg to the Orchestrator's key. L1's iss is the RFC 7638 thumbprint, which covers only the required members crv, kty and x (step 4c). PERMIT.
